name: Shiretoko Five Lakes (知床五湖)
why: Forest paths past five quiet lakes in brown bear country, then a raised boardwalk to the first lake with the Shiretoko range rising behind it.
book: Open mid-April to mid-November with the park road. The ground paths need a 10-minute lecture and a ticket (450 yen) at the Field House, sold 08:00-15:00; from 10 May to 31 July you may walk them only on a registered guide's tour (book ahead). They close when a bear is seen. The elevated boardwalk is free and always open in season.
water: Toilets and drinks at the Field House only. Carry water in a sealed bottle; no sugary drinks or open food on the ground paths.
dangers: Brown bears: if you see one, back away slowly, never run, and tell the Field House.
Muddy roots on the ground paths after rain.
Mosquitoes and cool wind by the lakes in summer.
turnaround: If a bear is reported, the staff close the ground paths: walk the elevated boardwalk instead.

points.name: Shiretoko Goko Field House
points.note: Lecture, tickets and guides at the entrance of the ground paths, 15 minutes by car from Utoro. The long loop goes round all five lakes.

points.name: Fifth lake
points.note: The first lake you reach on the long loop, the farthest from the road; then the fourth, third and second in the forest.

points.name: First lake and the Shiretoko range
points.note: The largest lake, with Mount Rausu and the Shiretoko range behind it. Walk back to the Field House on the 800 m elevated boardwalk, fenced against bears.
